items.q: What is corporate compliance in the UAE, and why is it important?
items.a: Corporate compliance in the UAE means fulfilling regulatory requirements — ESR, UBO, Corporate Tax, VAT, AML/CFT, and labour laws. It ensures your business remains licensed, banked, and legally protected.

items.q: Who must file Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the UAE?
items.a: ESR applies to businesses conducting relevant activities — consultancy, holding, shipping, financing, and IP. They must file notifications and ESR reports with the Ministry of Finance.

items.q: What happens if I miss my UBO filing deadlines?
items.a: Fines up to AED 100,000, license cancellation, and Free Zone or DED investigations. We help avoid this with accurate, on-time filings.

items.q: Is Corporate Tax mandatory for Free Zone companies?
items.a: Yes. Free Zone companies must register for Corporate Tax. Qualifying income may get 0% rate; non-qualifying income is taxed at 9%.

items.q: Do small businesses need compliance services in the UAE?
items.a: Absolutely. ESR, UBO, VAT, and WPS obligations apply to all registered businesses — regardless of size.

items.q: What is AML/CFT compliance, and who needs to comply?
items.a: Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Terrorism Financing. DNFBPs (real estate, legal, accounting, gold) must register goAML and appoint a Compliance Officer.

items.q: What is WPS, and how do I comply?
items.a: Wages Protection System. Employers must pay salaries through WPS-linked bank accounts and maintain MoHRE-compliant records.

items.q: Will you help during a government audit?
items.a: Yes. We prepare all documentation, represent you to MOF/FTA/MoHRE, and ensure a clean audit closure.

items.q: What are the penalties for non-compliance?
items.a: Fines up to AED 500,000+, license suspension, visa rejections, bank delays, and personal legal liability for directors.
